shelf: The public catalog: every course whose status is published, and nothing else.
place: An enrollment row, which is the record that a student may read a course, kept whether or not they ever open it.
open place: A place the student has not closed, so its course still appears on their list.
roster: A teacher's class list for one course: the students who hold a place, named and never emailed.
free preview: A lesson the teacher marked readable by anybody, so a stranger can open it without taking a place.
archive: Ends the course for everybody, including the students who hold a place in it.
series: A weekly class pattern a teacher writes down — a weekday, a start, an end and a length — which a sweep turns into dated classes.
dated class: One class with a day and an hour attached, written out from a series: the row a calendar is actually made of.
cohort class: A dated class a course scheduled for everyone holding a place in it, rather than one a student asked for.
register: The names beside one dated class — every student holding a place in its course — before anybody has marked who came.
roll: The register once the teacher has answered it — `present`, `absent`, or nothing beside a name nobody has marked — and not the roster, which is a course's whole class list.
holiday: A date a teacher marks off, once or every year, so none of their series runs that day.
slot: One bookable window of one teacher's calendar, refused to a second request once it is taken.
instant-book: A booking the system confirms the moment it is asked for rather than leaving it for the teacher.
retire: To take a row out of use by clearing its active flag, leaving the row and everything that points at it.
outbox: The queue of messages the platform means to send, delivered by a scheduled sweep rather than by the request that wrote it.
port: The name for the boundary an outside system sits behind, such as mail, video or storage, and not for a network socket.
redemption: One use of a coupon, counted against the cap the teacher set on it.
minor units: An amount stored as a count of the smallest unit of its currency, so 50000 read alongside INR is five hundred rupees.
